Hakolah — everything useful in Bahrain, in one place 👇

A Bahraini guide that gathers everything useful in one place: restaurants, cafés, stores, places, links and tools, and articles. For me, Hakolah is a turning point in what I know — new technologies I never dreamed I\'d hold in my hands.
Hakolah started out of curiosity: I wanted to explore AI tools and their ability to write code, and see how far I could go. And I\'m genuinely amazed.

Hakolah isn\'t the first site I\'ve built with AI — my personal website was the first — but it\'s the first thing I\'ve built with Claude Code specifically. A fascinating experience: I can make whatever I want with words and a little time. An indescribable feeling, and to this day I haven\'t lost the excitement or the passion.

string-array.name: story_stop_texts
string-array.item: The first version: sections, search, filters, favorites, and a control panel for adding content without writing code — plus the first real restaurant.
Likes shared across all visitors, stored by a small server on Cloudflare.
A strict security policy for the site, with every inline script removed.
Google AdSense rejected the site for \"low value content\" — and that same day, real detail pages were built for the items.
The car shops section, followed by dozens of new restaurants and stores.
\"Pick for me\" becomes an animated reveal that uncovers the suggestion piece by piece.
The \"AI Experiments\" section: small tools built with AI.
Work begins on a native Android app for Hakolah — the one in your hands right now.
A new look for the app: a 3D \"Pick for me\" sphere, the \"Today\'s picks\" stack, calm sounds, and a full English version.

string-array.name: story_tech_texts
string-array.item: I write what I want in words, and it turns into working code.
Builds fast, ready-made pages from simple files.
A control panel where I add a restaurant or a store from the browser.
Every change is published online automatically, for free.
A small server that keeps the like count for each item.
Every click you hear here is generated by code, without a single audio file.
This app: an interface built for touch, with content that updates itself from the site.

resources.string: A tough problem: I\'m building a project that takes part of my time without any income. But I\'ve come to understand that creating it is one step, making it work flawlessly is another, getting people to know it is a bigger step, and building an audience is bigger still — and growing the content matters too. So I\'m still working on it.
If you have any suggestion for Hakolah, tell me. And if you like it, share it with someone who needs it.
